original_value: Menstruation has long remained a conversational taboo across India, resulting in inadequate dissemination of menstrual health education (MHE). Menstrupedia, a digital platform designed for an Indian audience, aims to bridge this information gap to impart MHE via its website and comic. We contribute a study of Menstrupedia---the information exchange on its website, the education it aims to provide, and the perceptions of its users. Using a combination of qualitative research methods, and engaging a feminist Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) lens, we critically analyze Menstrupedia's affordances and shortcomings. We also make recommendations for the design of technology-based dissemination of MHE, as well as additional sensitive and taboo topics.

result.paraphrase: Across India, menstruation has long been a conversational taboo, which has led to poor dissemination of menstrual health education (MHE). Menstrupedia, a digital platform created for an Indian audience, seeks to close this information gap by delivering MHE through its website and comic. In this work, we examine Menstrupedia: the information exchange on its website, the education it intends to offer, and how users perceive it. Drawing on qualitative research methods and a feminist Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) perspective, we critically assess Menstrupedia’s strengths and limitations. We also propose design recommendations for technology-supported dissemination of MHE, along with other sensitive and taboo subjects.
